lede: Digits likelihood falls, then the inverse samples stay broken; Fashion was never trained.
title: Multi-scale RealNVP
question: Does the coupling flow assign high likelihood to MNIST and invert into digit-like samples?
process: The model is a convolutional RealNVP. A checkerboard-style mask holds one part fixed and two heads predict scale and shift, y = m·x + (1−m)·(x·exp(s) + t), with s bounded by scale·tanh. The log-determinant sums s only on the changed coordinates. Multi-scale squeezes space into channels and factors half of them out at 14×14 and at 7×7. Pixels in [0, 1] are dequantized and logit-transformed. The recorded search is 2 trials and 1 epoch on digits (hidden 64, 4 layers, scale 2, lr 0.001). The train stage is configured for 20 epochs and wrote loss, bits-per-dimension, and inverse-sample plots. It did not write evaluation JSON. Fashion stages exist in dvc.yaml and were not run.

opening.summary: The digits train plot shows negative log-likelihood and bits per dimension falling, then flattening, with the test curve under the train curve. The only numeric likelihood on disk is the search: validation BPD 1.583 after one epoch.

marks.label: Inverse samples, digits
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Inverting the flow does produce bright strokes on black, and a few cells suggest a loop or a stem. Most cells are hooks, specks, and broken junctions. Likelihood moved; the samples did not become a digit set.
marks.frameCaption: 64 inverse-flow samples from the digits train.

marks.label: Test evaluation
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The eval stage would have written test NLL and BPD. Those files are absent, so the plot is the likelihood record and there is no held-out number to quote beside the tune.

marks.label: Fashion-MNIST
marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: The same coupling stack was meant to train on Fashion from the same split. No fashion checkpoint, curve, or sample grid is in the tree, so there is no second dataset to compare.

reflection.worked: Coupling layers, the masked log-determinant, and the two squeeze scales are in the model, and the digits train does reduce bits per dimension before the curve flattens. The inverse pass runs and writes a 64-image grid.
reflection.unexpected: The grid is stroke fragments rather than digits. The search file and the train plots are different runs, and the test JSON never landed. Fashion is entirely absent.
reflection.why: A short search cannot place a 28×28 density on the digit manifold. Dequantization and the logit transform let likelihood improve by explaining background and rough stroke mass while individual glyphs stay off-manifold. About ten plotted epochs is still a short fit for this stack, and the missing eval means the flatten point was never frozen as a test score.
reflection.improve: Finish the 20-epoch digits train, write evaluation_test.json, and keep a sample grid every few epochs next to BPD. Then run the fashion train and eval with the same depth. If BPD keeps falling while samples stay broken, check the masked log-det and how many channels the squeezes factor out before adding more layers.
